Subject: Integration and connectivity follow-up — Helio Health

Hi Rajiv,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Per our call I pulled together a short starter plan that covers the integration work we discussed: SDK integration, auth, structured outputs/tool-calling, embeddings/reranker flow, and the private connectivity pieces (VPC endpoints, IP allowlists, egress/DNS, and mTLS). Attached: helio_integration_checklist.pdf (checklist + owner table).

Summary (high level)
- SDK: recommend server-side SDK with short-lived API keys for inference calls; we can provide a reference Express/Flask snippet.
- Auth: two options — API key + IP allowlist for initial POC, or mutual TLS (mTLS) for production-grade isolation.
- Routing: per-tenant routing using Redwood routing tags; can pin to dedicated variants for low-latency paths.
- Structured output / tool-calling: Redwood supports JSON-schema constrained outputs and direct tool-calling hooks (webhook + signed callback). We suggest a small set of guarded tool-call scopes for POC.
- Embeddings & reranker: embeddings can be hosted via the same private link; recommend batch embed pipeline + reranker endpoint co-located to minimize egress.
- Networking: two deployment patterns — (A) VPC Endpoint (recommended) with private egress to our dedicated pool; (B) IP allowlist + TLS egress (simpler but less isolated). Both support DNS resolution for model hosts.

Action items / proposed next steps
1) Helio to confirm whether you want POC as Option A (VPC Endpoint) or Option B (IP allowlist).
2) If VPC Endpoint: share VPC id, preferred subnet, and contact for network ops; we’ll provide CloudFormation/ARM snippets.
3) If IP allowlist: confirm outbound egress IPs and DNS fallback rules; procurement to confirm any required DPA/SLA terms.
4) We’ll schedule a 60-min technical working session next week to walk through the checklist and run the SDK quickstart. Please propose 2x 60-min blocks.

Attached: helio_integration_checklist.pdf, egress_policy_example.txt

Thanks — I’ll coordinate if procurement wants a separate thread for contract items.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Rajiv — good questions, answering inline below.

1) VPC Endpoint routing: the recommended pattern is a VPC Interface Endpoint (private link style). That keeps traffic within the VPC and does not require changing your NAT/gateway for egress to Redwood. We will provide the endpoint DNS names and a short CloudFormation template to create the interface endpoint and associated security group.

2) mTLS cert rotation: Redwood supports two modes — (a) Redwood-managed certs where we handle issuance and rotation (customers approve rotation windows); or (b) customer-managed certificates via HashiCorp Vault (we accept a signed client cert during the TLS handshake). HashiCorp integration is supported via a short-lived cert exchange: you can push certs to our onboarding API or use your CA to issue certs that we trust. We will share an example cert-rotation playbook.

3) Embeddings/reranker latency: colocating the reranker with the embedding store typically yields 20–60ms additional latency for a 1–2k embedding vector space if running on a dedicated pool. For UI result targets ~200ms, we recommend pinning the reranker to a dedicated variant and enabling our in-process caching layer (reduces repeated queries). Exact numbers depend on model size and batch size — we’ll include benchmarking commands in the checklist.

Additional notes:
- IP allowlist POC: we can start with this for an isolated sandbox while you validate model outputs. Production we recommend VPC Endpoint + mTLS for stronger guarantees.
- DNS: the VPC endpoint resolves to an internal hostname; we recommend adding a CNAME in your private zone if you want friendly names.

Next step: can you confirm preferred POC path by EOD Monday (May 24)? If you pick VPC Endpoint, please share a network contact and a sample subnet ID.

Best,
Naomi
